mappings.supportedSubset: Double-precision scalar and one-dimensional vector addition or subtraction, numeric input-count shorthand, elementwise equal-width multi-input vectors, and all-elements reduction for a one-port vector.
intentionalDeviations: Process Lab authors signal width explicitly because it does not yet implement diagram-wide inherited dimension propagation.
Mixed scalar and vector input expansion, matrices, spacer characters, specified-dimension reduction, data-type accumulation policy, saturation, and fixed-point behavior are outside this subset.

mappings.supportedSubset: Scalar or one-dimensional vector signals delayed by one explicit or run-inherited sample period, with scalar-broadcast or width-matched finite initial conditions.
intentionalDeviations: Process Lab authors vector width explicitly instead of inheriting signal dimensions.
Frame-based processing, data types other than double, state naming, and code-generation options are outside this subset.

mappings.supportedSubset: Elementwise signed addition of equal-width vectors with explicit input and output channel labels.
intentionalDeviations: Vector Sum retains explicit named channels and is not the direct Sum counterpart.
A single Vector Sum input is passed elementwise instead of applying Simulink Sum-of-elements reduction.

mappings.supportedSubset: Collect scalar ports into one explicitly named vector.
intentionalDeviations: Channel labels are Process-Lab-authored routing metadata rather than inherited Simulink signal attributes.

mappings.supportedSubset: Split one explicitly named vector into scalar ports.
intentionalDeviations: Channel labels are Process-Lab-authored routing metadata rather than inherited Simulink signal attributes.

mappings.supportedSubset: Select channels by authored names and order.
intentionalDeviations: Process Lab uses names instead of Simulink index and dimension parameters.

mappings.supportedSubset: Reorder every named channel exactly once.
intentionalDeviations: Permutation is a Process-Lab-specific convenience abstraction without a single direct Simulink block counterpart.

mappings.supportedSubset: Emit a finite vector with explicit channel names.
intentionalDeviations: Named channels are authored as block parameters.

mappings.supportedSubset: Apply a constant matrix to an explicitly named input vector and emit explicitly named outputs.
intentionalDeviations: Process Lab fixes matrix multiplication orientation and authors channel names explicitly.

mappings.supportedSubset: Persist every channel of one explicitly named vector input.
intentionalDeviations: Vector Scope is a Process-Lab-specific persisted-result sink rather than a full Simulink Scope.
